central_hypothesis: As mainland access weakens, ecologically relevant source context shifts from mainland-anchored isolation toward continuity with the occupied insular source network.

ecological_states.mainland_source_rich: climate, island area, mainland distance and direct/diffuse focal-source context explain most held-out occurrence support; species-conditioned topology is mostly redundant
ecological_states.remote_and_unlinked: generic mainland access is weak and no compensating occupied insular source path is present
ecological_states.remote_but_linked: generic mainland access is weak but the focal species remains connected to occupied insular sources through the frozen archipelago graph

interpretation: island area and classical mainland/source isolation dominate ordinary occurrence support
widespread species show stronger topology redundancy under ordinary conditions, consistent with source saturation
mainland remoteness rather than island area moderates the residual topology signal
extreme remoteness creates a split between remote-but-linked and remote-and-unlinked source states
multi-hop occupied source continuity contains information not reducible to direct nearest-source distance
the effective source context may shift from mainland access toward archipelago-internal occupied source continuity
claim_ceiling: no realized dispersal route is observed
no contemporary colonization probability is estimated
no rescue effect or demographic persistence is demonstrated
no universal mainland-distance threshold is claimed
